name: Contrastive Chain-of-Thought
executive_summary: Show both valid AND invalid worked reasoning examples, so the model learns what mistakes to avoid, not just what correct reasoning looks like — plain CoT only ever demonstrates success.
description: Motivated by a surprising prior finding: plain CoT's benefit barely drops even when the demonstrated reasoning is logically invalid, suggesting the model isn't learning as much from the demonstrations' correctness as assumed. Contrastive CoT addresses this directly by pairing each valid reasoning demonstration with an invalid one showing a specific, plausible mistake, with an automatic method for constructing the contrastive (invalid) demonstrations rather than requiring hand-authored ones.
when_to_use: Reasoning tasks with a known, common class of mistake worth explicitly demonstrating and warning against.
when_not_to_use: Tasks with no clear 'common mistake' pattern to contrast against — constructing meaningful invalid demonstrations may not be straightforward.
known_pitfalls: Poorly chosen invalid demonstrations (unrealistic or off-target mistakes) may fail to transfer to the actual errors the model tends to make.
